claude.country: International (14 countries: Italy, Austria, Germany, UK, Switzerland, Canada, USA, Australia, and others)

links.outcome: Readability of original ChatGPT and evidence-based patient responses versus recommended patient reading levels
links.effect: Original ChatGPT median FKGL 12.60, ARI 15.35, FRE 41.95; evidence-based FKGL 11.50, ARI 14.15; both above the 11-12 year-old recommended level; differences not significant (FRE p=0.053).
links.quote: Since, based on these scores, both evidence-based responses and the initial ChatGPT responses appear to be at a complexity level which is generally challenging for the average reader, we prompted ChatGPT to simplify the provided responses.

links.outcome: Change in readability scores after prompting ChatGPT to simplify responses
links.effect: Simplified answers improved: FRE 41.95 to 57.77, FKGL 12.60 to 8.55, GFI 12.93 to 10.63, ARI 15.35 to 11.20 (p<0.01 for all versus evidence-based).
links.quote: Accordingly, all readability scores improved significantly for the ChatGPT simplified answers ( p < 0.01 for all analyses) ( Table 4 ).

unlisted_practices: Prompting LLM to simplify responses on user request to improve readability

links.effect: ChatGPT higher for 11/12 questions; r_rb=-0.46 to -1.00; all p<0.05; +0.824 units average.
links.quote: ChatGPT responses were rated significantly higher than the evidence-based responses for 11 of the 12 study questions, with moderate to large effect sizes (r r b  = -0.46 to -1.00; all p-values <0.05), with ChatGPT answers being rated on average 0.824 units higher.

links.effect: Weighted κ ranged from −0.03 to 0.37; agreement was poor to fair.
links.quote: Weighted Kappa ( κ ) with quadratic weights computed for each of the 12 study questions showed that the level of agreement varied across questions, ranging from poor to fair agreement ( Figure 3 ).
Accordingly, all readability scores improved significantly for the ChatGPT simplified answers ( p < 0.01 for all analyses) ( Table 4 ).

links.effect: EB vs original ChatGPT: FKGL 11.50 vs 12.60; ARI 14.15 vs 15.35; FRE 49.41 vs 41.95.
links.quote: Moreover, the performed readability analyses on all responses to the study questions consistently indicate that both the evidence-based and the initial ChatGPT responses required a higher level of health literacy, potentially exceeding the current readability recommendations for the general patient information.

links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-generated PCOS self-management responses
links.effect: Initial ChatGPT responses had median FKGL of 12.60, GFI of 12.93, ARI of 15.35, and FRE of 41.95, indicating text complexity exceeding recommended reading levels for general patient information.
links.quote: Moreover, the performed readability analyses on all responses to the study questions consistently indicate that both the evidence-based and the initial ChatGPT responses required a higher level of health literacy, potentially exceeding the current readability recommendations for the general patient information.

screen.reason: Evaluated ChatGPT responses to patient FAQ questions on PCOS compared to evidence-based online responses via healthcare professional survey, and specifically tested the effect of using ChatGPT for simplifying the responses (readability/simplification constraints).
